Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. ## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give the believer a name, and the works disagree on it.
- Which Yusuf is meant in the believer's words is not stated by the Quran beyond the name.
- Hadith to add later: reports about the believer from the family of Fir'awn, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. A believer speaks  (`#a-believer-speaks`)

Cited ayat: 40:28-29

> **40:28** وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُۥٓ أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ وَقَدْ جَآءَكُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ وَإِن يَكُ كَٰذِبًا فَعَلَيْهِ كَذِبُهُۥ وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ كَذَّابٌ
>
> **40:29** يَٰقَوْمِ لَكُمُ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْمَ ظَٰهِرِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَمَن يَنصُرُنَا مِنۢ بَأْسِ ٱللَّهِ إِن جَآءَنَا قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ مَآ أُرِيكُمْ إِلَّا مَآ أَرَىٰ وَمَآ أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ

### Claims

**c1** (40:28): A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who concealed his belief, asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God, when he had come to them with clear proofs from their Lord, adding that if he was lying his lie would be on him, and if he was truthful, some of what he promised would befall them, and that God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.

**c2** (40:29): He said that the kingdom was theirs that day, prevailing in the land, and asked who would help them against the might of God if it came to them, and Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw and guided them only to the way of right conduct.

### One-minute summary

A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who concealed his belief, asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God [c1]. He asked who would help them against God's might if it came [c2]. Fir'awn answered that he showed them only what he saw [c2].

### Complete story

A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who concealed his belief, asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God, when he had come to them with clear proofs from their Lord, adding that if he was lying his lie would be on him, and if he was truthful, some of what he promised would befall them, and that God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar [c1]. He said that the kingdom was theirs that day, prevailing in the land, and asked who would help them against the might of God if it came to them, and Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw and guided them only to the way of right conduct [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah says that he concealed his belief, and it does not say why he now spoke [c1]. Neither the believer nor the man he speaks of is named in this ayah [c1].

### Kids mode

A believing man in the family of Fir'awn spoke up [c1]. He asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God [c1]. Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the believer argues that a lie would fall on the liar and a truth would bring some of what is promised [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the believer's name, his rank or his kinship to Fir'awn.
- Not established: how long he had concealed his belief, or how it came to be known.
- Not established in this ayah: who the man is whom the believer defends.

## 2. Warnings from the past  (`#warnings-from-the-past`)

Cited ayat: 40:30-35

> **40:30** وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُم مِّثْلَ يَوْمِ ٱلْأَحْزَابِ
>
> **40:31** مِثْلَ دَأْبِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعَادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْمًا لِّلْعِبَادِ
>
> **40:32** وَيَٰقَوْمِ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلتَّنَادِ
>
> **40:33** يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ مَا لَكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍ وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
>
> **40:34** وَلَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِن قَبْلُ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ فَمَا زِلْتُمْ فِى شَكٍّ مِّمَّا جَآءَكُم بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَن يَبْعَثَ ٱللَّهُ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ رَسُولًا كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ مُّرْتَابٌ
>
> **40:35** ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِىٓ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطَٰنٍ أَتَىٰهُمْ كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَعِندَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكَ يَطْبَعُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ قَلْبِ مُتَكَبِّرٍ جَبَّارٍ

### Claims

**c1** (40:30-31): The believer said that he feared for them a day like the day of the factions, like the fate of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud and those after them, and that God does not wish injustice for His servants.

**c2** (40:32-33): He said that he feared for them the day of mutual calling, the day when they would turn back, with no protector for them from God, and that whoever God lets go astray has no guide.

**c3** (40:34): He said that Yusuf had come to them before with clear proofs, yet they remained in doubt about what he brought, and when he died they said that God would never send a messenger after him, and that thus God lets go astray the transgressor, the doubter.

**c4** (40:35): He said of those who dispute God's signs without any authority that this is greatly hateful to God and to those who believe, and that thus God seals every arrogant, tyrannical heart.

### One-minute summary

The believer warned them of a day like the day of the factions, like the fate of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud [c1]. He spoke of the day when they would turn back with no protector from God [c2]. He said that Yusuf had come to them before with clear proofs, yet they remained in doubt [c3].

### Complete story

The believer said that he feared for them a day like the day of the factions, like the fate of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud and those after them, and that God does not wish injustice for His servants [c1]. He said that he feared for them the day of mutual calling, the day when they would turn back, with no protector for them from God, and that whoever God lets go astray has no guide [c2]. He said that Yusuf had come to them before with clear proofs, yet they remained in doubt about what he brought, and when he died they said that God would never send a messenger after him, and that thus God lets go astray the transgressor, the doubter [c3]. He said of those who dispute God's signs without any authority that this is greatly hateful to God and to those who believe, and that thus God seals every arrogant, tyrannical heart [c4].

### Deep study

The believer names earlier peoples as warnings [c1] and then speaks of Yusuf [c3]. The ayah does not say which Yusuf is meant beyond the name, nor when he came to them [c3].

### Kids mode

The believer reminded them of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud [c1]. He said that Yusuf had come to them with clear proofs, yet they stayed in doubt [c3]. He said that God does not wish injustice for His servants [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the believer's warnings begin with earlier peoples and end with a messenger whose proofs they doubted [c1][c3]. Another is that he describes those who dispute God's signs without authority as greatly hated by God and by the believers [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which Yusuf is meant; the ayah gives only the name and says that he came with clear proofs.
- Not established: when Yusuf came to them, or how long he was among them.
- Not established: what the day of the factions or the day of mutual calling mean beyond the words of the ayat.

## 3. Follow me  (`#follow-me`)

Cited ayat: 40:38-45

> **40:38** وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَامَنَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ
>
> **40:39** يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا مَتَٰعٌ وَإِنَّ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ هِىَ دَارُ ٱلْقَرَارِ
>
> **40:40** مَنْ عَمِلَ سَيِّئَةً فَلَا يُجْزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَمَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ يُرْزَقُونَ فِيهَا بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
>
> **40:41** وَيَٰقَوْمِ مَا لِىٓ أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى ٱلنَّجَوٰةِ وَتَدْعُونَنِىٓ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ
>
> **40:42** تَدْعُونَنِى لِأَكْفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَأُشْرِكَ بِهِۦ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَأَنَا۠ أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْغَفَّٰرِ
>
> **40:43** لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّمَا تَدْعُونَنِىٓ إِلَيْهِ لَيْسَ لَهُۥ دَعْوَةٌ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَلَا فِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ وَأَنَّ مَرَدَّنَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَنَّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ هُمْ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ
>
> **40:44** فَسَتَذْكُرُونَ مَآ أَقُولُ لَكُمْ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَصِيرٌۢ بِٱلْعِبَادِ
>
> **40:45** فَوَقَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِ مَا مَكَرُوا۟ وَحَاقَ بِـَٔالِ فِرْعَوْنَ سُوٓءُ ٱلْعَذَابِ

### Claims

**c1** (40:38-40): He said, my people, follow me, I will guide you to the way of right conduct, this life is only enjoyment and the Hereafter is the home of settlement, whoever does an evil deed is repaid only the like of it, while whoever does righteous work, male or female, and is a believer, those enter the Garden, provided for without reckoning.

**c2** (40:41-43): He asked why he called them to salvation while they called him to the Fire, said that they called him to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him what he had no knowledge of, while he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving, and said that what they called him to has no claim in this world or the Hereafter, that their return is to God, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.

**c3** (40:44): He said that they would remember what he told them, and that he committed his affair to God, who sees His servants.

**c4** (40:45): God protected him from the evil of what they plotted, and the worst punishment enveloped the family of Fir'awn.

### One-minute summary

The believer asked them to follow him, and said that he would guide them to the way of right conduct [c1]. He said that he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving, while they called him to the Fire [c2]. He committed his affair to God, who protected him from the evil of what they plotted [c3][c4].

### Complete story

He said, my people, follow me, I will guide you to the way of right conduct, this life is only enjoyment and the Hereafter is the home of settlement, whoever does an evil deed is repaid only the like of it, while whoever does righteous work, male or female, and is a believer, those enter the Garden, provided for without reckoning [c1]. He asked why he called them to salvation while they called him to the Fire, said that they called him to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him what he had no knowledge of, while he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving, and said that what they called him to has no claim in this world or the Hereafter, that their return is to God, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire [c2]. He said that they would remember what he told them, and that he committed his affair to God, who sees His servants [c3]. God protected him from the evil of what they plotted, and the worst punishment enveloped the family of Fir'awn [c4].

### Deep study

The believer speaks of this life as enjoyment and of the Hereafter as the home of settlement [c1]. The pronoun in the words God protected him is not spelled out, and the ayah does not say whom it refers to beyond the speaker [c4].

### Kids mode

The believer asked his people to follow him [c1]. He said that he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving [c2]. He committed his affair to God, who sees His servants [c3]. God protected him from the evil of what they plotted [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the believer ends by committing his affair to God and that the ayah then says God protected him [c3][c4]. Another is that he contrasts calling to the Garden and calling to the Fire [c1][c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what became of the believer after these words, beyond the statement that God protected him from the evil of what they plotted.
- Not established: who is meant by him in the words God protected him; the ayah leaves it open.
- Not established: whether the people answered him, or how.
